title: Find the Position of @ in Email Addresses
description:
Write a query that returns `id`, `name`, `email`, and the character position of `'@'` in the email as `at_position`.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| email | VARCHAR |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 'alice@company.com'), (2, 'Bob', 'bob.smith@company.com'), (3, 'Carol', 'carol@techcorp.com'), (4, 'Diana', 'diana.prince@company.com'), (5, 'Evan', 'evan@startup.io'), (6, 'Frank', 'frank.w@techcorp.com');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, email, POSITION('@' IN email) AS at_position FROM employees

test_cases.description: Returns 6 rows with the position of @ in each email address

hints: `POSITION('substring' IN column)` returns the 1-based index of the first occurrence. Returns 0 if not found.
In MySQL you can also use `INSTR(email, '@')` — it works identically.
explanation: `POSITION('@' IN email)` finds where the @ symbol sits in each email. alice@ is at position 6, bob.smith@ at 10, carol@ at 6, diana.prince@ at 13, evan@ at 5, frank.w@ at 8.
